cases.title: Meet My Family
cases.focus: Family relationships, family and social roles, mutual respect and shared responsibilities.

text_rows.title: Family Album
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Value the family and experience affection.
text_rows.language_focus: Ask about and introduce family membership; connect kinship vocabulary with its sound, spelling and meaning in context.
skills_and_strategies: Predict theme, context and main information from images and title.
Learn vocabulary through sound, written form and contextual meaning.

text_rows.title: Jobs of Family Members
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Family members have roles both at home and in society.
text_rows.language_focus: Ask about and introduce occupations and appearance.
skills_and_strategies: Ask and answer questions about family members.

text_rows.title: June Sings
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Family members should understand and respect one another and offer support and encouragement.
text_rows.language_focus: Discuss respectful behaviour, family activities and emotions.
skills_and_strategies: Predict the main story information from images and title.
Interpret meaning in images, colours and sound.
Use images and major language patterns to recount the story.

text_rows.title: My Family
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Contribute to family and society while showing love for the family.
text_rows.language_focus: Describe family activities, occupations and contributions.
skills_and_strategies: Use a scaffold moving from overall introduction to parents’ occupations, individual contributions and a closing summary.

objectives.summary: Exchange information with classmates and introduce one’s family members, including appearance and occupations.
Individually or collaboratively design advice cards about creating harmonious family relationships.
Follow a model to introduce family members using pictures and text, including appearance, work and home responsibilities, while expressing feelings about the family.

lesson_sequence.title: Family Album
lesson_sequence.task: Introduce and ask about family members using an album.

lesson_sequence.title: Jobs of Family Members
lesson_sequence.task: Ask about and describe family members’ occupations.
lesson_sequence.thematic_connection: Extend awareness of family members’ social roles.

lesson_sequence.title: June Sings
lesson_sequence.task: Discuss family rules and create advice for respectful, supportive relationships.
lesson_sequence.thematic_connection: Understand mutual care, support and encouragement.

lesson_sequence.title: My Family
lesson_sequence.task: Introduce family members and their contributions with an illustrated description.
lesson_sequence.thematic_connection: Take family responsibilities and express love.

progression.description: Move from identifying people and roles to interpreting respectful relationships and expressing personal responsibility; comprehension and expression develop together across the four texts.

project.english_paraphrase: Create and share a family album expressing love for one’s family.
project.integration: Figure3 links the four lessons through three subthemes and then through this shared project before the final respect-and-care synthesis.

assessment.description: Observable evidence comes from information exchange, family-harmony advice cards and an illustrated family introduction. The family album is also an explicit integrative figure project.

opportunities.evidence: Family information exchange and introductions covering relevant appearance and work.
Advice cards explaining how family members should treat one another.
An illustrated introduction linking family facts, responsibilities and feelings.

assessment.caveat: These are curriculum classroom outcomes and evidence opportunities, not a printed scored rubric or city-exam rule.

cases.title: Do Family Chores
cases.focus: Household work, responsibility, practical participation, planning and enjoyment of useful work.

text_rows.title: Do You Do Chores at Home?
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Household work is a responsibility that primary pupils should undertake.
skills_and_strategies: Ask and answer questions about chores.
Use pictures and title to predict context and how events develop.

text_rows.title: What Chores Do You Do at Home?
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Actively share household work and develop awareness of its value.
skills_and_strategies: Extract and organize information about time, people and the course of events while viewing and listening.

text_rows.title: Charlie’s Chores
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Share chores actively, enjoy working and balance school, life and household responsibilities.
text_rows.language_focus: Express and explain attitudes toward doing chores.
skills_and_strategies: Extract and organize characters’ chores while listening and reading.

text_rows.title: Robots
text_rows.thematic_meaning: Robots can make life easier, while pupils still need practical life skills and the enjoyment of doing useful work.
text_rows.language_focus: Describe a robot and its possible help or services.
skills_and_strategies: Locate paragraph topic sentences and connect them with supporting content.
Draw a creative robot and use short written and spoken descriptions to present it.

objectives.summary: Exchange information in a group, record personal plans for next week’s chores and present the plans to the class.
Learn or carry out a household task, record it in a preferred form and present the record to classmates.
Describe how the main character’s attitude toward chores changes.
Exchange personal chore experiences and feelings with classmates.
Design and present a robot, describing its appearance and the services or help it could provide.
Discuss why pupils still need to learn chores when robots can help with household work.

lesson_sequence.title: Do You Do Chores at Home?
lesson_sequence.task: Discuss after-school choices and exchange and record plans for household work.

lesson_sequence.title: What Chores Do You Do at Home?
lesson_sequence.task: Exchange familiar chores and feelings; learn or perform a task and present a record of doing it.

lesson_sequence.title: Charlie’s Chores
lesson_sequence.task: Describe the character’s attitude change and reflect on one’s own willingness to contribute.

lesson_sequence.title: Robots
lesson_sequence.task: Design and describe a helpful robot, then discuss why learning chores remains valuable.

progression.description: Use understanding, application/practice and transfer/innovation across connected contexts; link personal plans and practical participation with reflection and evaluation of technology.
figure_subthemes: Primary pupils should undertake household work.
Balance learning, daily life and chores.
Enjoy work and experience the happiness it creates.

project.english_paraphrase: Create and share a poster presenting oneself as a helpful contributor at home.
project.integration: A new poster-project layer links the four lessons and subthemes to the concluding responsibility-and-joy synthesis.

assessment.description: The six objectives provide observable evidence through a next-week plan, a record of practical work, attitude explanations, personal reflection, a robot presentation and a reasoned discussion. The family-helper poster is an additional explicit figure project.

opportunities.evidence: Recorded chore plans and a group/class presentation.
A record and presentation of actually learning or carrying out a chore.
An explanation of the character’s changing attitude and personal experience exchange.
A robot design/presentation and a discussion of the continuing need for life skills.

assessment.caveat: The source supplies classroom goals, not marks or analytic performance bands. Doing a project alone does not establish independent mastery.

substantive_changes: Content table adds explicit thematic meaning and combines language examples into one column.
Figure4 moves from theme through lessons and subthemes to a new shared family-helper poster project.
Selected household-work expressions and the listed telephone-language example change; details are recorded in changes.json.
